clue.text: O Kelvin, it's cold!

blocks.note: surface reading: a cheery remark addressed to someone named Kelvin about the weather
setter's reading: zero on the Kelvin scale, the coldest temperature possible

explanation.walkthrough: The O looks like an exclamation to a person called Kelvin; it stands for the figure 0 on the Kelvin temperature scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute zero is the theoretical lowest temperature, defined as nought on the Kelvin scale.

clue.text: The woman can return annual workbook

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the word before it is read from its end

blocks.note: taken as a woman's name, Alma
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: A woman is able to hand back her yearly exercise book.
explanation.walkthrough: The woman is a specific woman's name, Alma, rather than SHE or HER.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a reference book published every year, with calendars, tables and statistics.

clue.text: Ruined when polished carelessly, but not hard

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter standing for hard is taken out
done carelessly, the letters fall out of their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A finish was spoilt by careless polishing, though the surface is not hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoiled is a past participle meaning damaged or ruined, matching ruined exactly.

clue.text: Cliff fall in Iceland slid eventually into the sea

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows this little word

blocks.note: the letters run from the middle of the first word across the second into the start of the third
surface padding that completes the picture of a coastal collapse

explanation.surface: Part of a cliff in Iceland gave way and slipped into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The closing words into the sea complete the picture of a coastal collapse and add nothing to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslide is a mass of earth and rock collapsing down a slope, as when a cliff gives way.

clue.text: Taken for granted when understood

blocks.note: first meaning: assumed without being stated
second meaning: implied rather than spoken aloud

explanation.surface: Something is assumed once everyone grasps it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit agreement is unspoken and implied, so it is both assumed and silently understood.

clue.text: Keen (but jealous) judge leaves as last character's taken on

indicators.text: leaves as last character's taken on
indicators.note: one letter departs and another is brought in to fill its place

blocks.note: taken as written
J is the abbreviation for judge, and it is the letter that leaves
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An eager but envious judge quits when the final candidate is hired.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the J of JEALOUS for Z, the alphabet's last character.
explanation.definitionFit: Zealous means full of enthusiasm and eager, a close synonym of keen.

clue.text: Finery from Algeria, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word is only a possible version of itself, its letters in some other order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fine clothing imported from Algeria, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia is ceremonial dress and insignia, splendid finery worn on formal occasions.

clue.text: Royal house agent moves English plants outside

indicators.note: when letters move about they end up in a new order
one word goes outside the others, wrapping around them

blocks.note: taken as written, split to wrap around the rest
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A spy from a royal household relocates some English plants.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plantagenets were the dynasty of English kings from Henry II to Richard III.

clue.text: Make fun of diving bird that swallowed torn map

indicators.note: something torn is ripped apart, so its letters are rearranged
what is swallowed ends up inside the swallower

blocks.note: the loon is a diving bird, called a diver in Britain
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mock the diving bird that gulped down a ripped map.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon is to ridicule someone through satire, the same as making fun of them.

clue.text: Given responsibility for church, dear? Good manoeuvre!

indicators.note: a manoeuvre is a change of position, so these letters are moved about

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone is handed control of a church and praised for a clever move.
explanation.definitionFit: Being charged with something means being entrusted with the duty of it, so given responsibility for it.

clue.text: Boring delay making a boundary construction

blocks.note: dull, tedious
to stonewall is to hold things up by obstruction

explanation.surface: A tedious hold-up while a boundary is being built.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry-stone wall is a field boundary built from stones fitted together without mortar.

clue.text: Fox no one heard, on the positive side

indicators.note: something heard is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: no one means none, spelt here by sound
plus is the positive sign

explanation.surface: Nobody heard a fox, which looks on the bright side.
explanation.walkthrough: Fox is the verb meaning to baffle, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to bewilder them, just as to fox someone is to baffle them.

clue.text: Cart to go round, yet return outside

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word is read from its end
the turned word goes outside the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: to roll is to turn over and over
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: A cart has to circle round, but then come back.
explanation.definitionFit: A trolley is a small wheeled cart, as in a supermarket or airport.

clue.text: Raced around, then bowed

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dashed about and then took a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Arced means curved into an arc, and something bowed is bent into a curve.

clue.text: Small article involved in illegal relationship that's on-going

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be inside it

blocks.note: sexual relations between close relatives, which the law forbids
S is the abbreviation for small
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A minor news piece about an illicit affair that continues.
explanation.definitionFit: Incessant means continuing without pause, so it is ongoing.

clue.text: Sudden restriction on vice by Irish county

blocks.note: a vice is a gripping tool, like a clamp
County Down is in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: An Irish county suddenly cracks down on wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: Vice looks like wrongdoing, which a crackdown would target, but it is the workshop tool; the on is part of that block's surface and adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A clampdown is an abrupt firm restriction imposed by an authority.

clue.text: Respiratory disorder my sheep inflicted on mother

indicators.note: something inflicted is forced on by violence, so the letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
MA is a familiar word for mother, placed after

explanation.surface: A lung complaint that my flock passed on to my mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphysema is a lung disease that damages the air sacs and causes breathlessness.

clue.text: Country lover's pet's disorder

blocks.note: to pet an animal is to pat it
a riot is public disorder

explanation.surface: A rural person's pet has some ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot loves and supports their own country.

clue.text: New guy, Nero, is not so old

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so these letters are remade in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The fresh recruit, Nero, is youthful.
explanation.definitionFit: Younger is the comparative of young, meaning of lesser age than another.

clue.text: Teacher's directions are a warning signal

blocks.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir; the 's means has
E and N, east and north, two compass directions

explanation.surface: A teacher's instructions are a caution to the class.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a device sounding a loud wail to warn of danger.

clue.text: Her Majesty seen at the back of the vessel, in a more serious mood

blocks.note: the stern is the rear of a ship
ER is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The Queen appears at the rear of the ship, looking rather grave.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names ER first but places her at the back, so the vessel's part comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterner is the comparative of stern, meaning more severe or grim.

clue.text: It's catastrophic, when promissory notes run out

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are out of place

blocks.note: IOUs are written promises to pay
taken as written

explanation.surface: It's a disaster when you run out of credit notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruinous means causing ruin or disaster, so it is catastrophic.

clue.text: Give custody to charge

blocks.note: first meaning: hand something over to be looked after
second meaning: to give someone a duty or task

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a court handing a defendant over, but each half is a separate meaning of one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrust is to place something in another's care, or to charge them with a responsibility.

clue.text: Heavyweight in charge of medicine

blocks.note: a ton is a heavy weight
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A big boxer has charge of the drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is a medicine meant to restore strength and well-being.

clue.text: Quiet appraisal of trailer

blocks.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
a review is a critical assessment

explanation.surface: A low-key assessment of a film trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailer gives a preview, an advance showing of extracts from a film.

clue.text: A little bit of a small insect? Point to it!

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a midge is a tiny biting fly
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone spots a speck of a tiny bug and says show me where.
explanation.walkthrough: The words of a and to it only join the pieces; point is a compass point added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgen is a very small amount, a tiny bit.

clue.text: The team's mistake was to confess an aim

blocks.note: to own up is to admit
a goal is an aim

explanation.surface: A team's blunder was admitting its objective.
explanation.definitionFit: An own goal is scored by a player into their own net, a mistake that benefits the other side.

clue.text: Recent development in disturbances at focal points of agitation

indicators.note: a development changes how something is laid out, so the letters are reworked
the reworked letters go inside the next word

blocks.note: storms are uproars or upheavals
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new twist in some unrest at the hotspots of protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Storm centres are places where trouble or controversy is most intense, like the eye of a storm.
